title: About
text:
These databases and pipelines are the result of a long-term collaboration across taxonomists, bioinformaticians, and ecologists to establish robust and user-friendly databases and pipelines for environmental identification of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF). AMF associate with 80% of plant species worldwide, impacting plant growth, survival, community structure, and ecosystem function. AMF are not one homogenous group; AMF taxa have variable impacts on their plant hosts and terrestrial ecosystem function. Still, their biodiversity is poorly understood. We hope these open databases and pipelines help increase our understanding of AMF diversity, ecology, and biogeography.
We are continuously updating the LSU database and pipeline. Currently, an ESIIL working group is supporting our continued work to (1) develop the first curated long-read AMF database, (2) build robust, open-access phylogenetic pipelines for AMF identification across major gene regions; and (3) apply these novel tools to reassess global distribution patterns of AMF. Find more information here: https://esiil.org/working-groups/amf-biogeography-diversity
Please contact us with any questions, bugs, or suggestions!

title: GloDB
text:
Welcome to GloDB! Here, you can find resources related to arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal (AMF) large subunit (LSU) and long-read PacBio (SSU-ITS-LSU) databases and associated pipelines. The databases rely on sequencing from culture collections, and are curated in collaboration with taxonomists. The LSU pipelines allow placement of study sequences into a LSU backbone tree to identify putative AMF (phylum Glomeromycota) as well as family and genera. These can be implemented for both operational taxonomic units (OTUs) or or amplicon sequence variants (ASVs). The original pipelines are built for computing clusters, but a recent version also allows for use outside of a cluster environment.
GloDB Backbone tree. A visualization of the latest curated LSU database backbone tree, including more than 400 tips with updated taxonomy. Colors show AMF genera (with grey representing outgroups).
LSU tree from curated long-read database LongGloDB. The LSU region was extracted from the PacBio long-reads to place them into the previously developed backbone LSU tree. Colors show database groups and AMF family.
